initialContact.message: I've been thinking about what would happen to my kids if something happened to me. I pay child support and try to be involved, but I don't have much saved. If I died, they'd get nothing. I looked into life insurance (henkivakuutus) but it's expensive - like 35€/month for 100,000€ coverage. Is it worth it? Or should I just try to save more? My ex would probably say I should have insurance but we don't really talk about this stuff.

problemContext.currentSituation: Divorced father concerned about providing for children if he dies, weighing life insurance costs
problemContext.emotionalState: worried, guilt, wanting to do right thing for kids, financial pressure

idealAdvice: This shows you're thinking responsibly about your children's future
Life insurance most valuable when you have dependents and limited savings - exactly your situation
35€/month for 100k coverage is reasonable for your age and situation
Term life insurance (määräaikainen henkivakuutus) is cheapest option for pure protection
Coverage should roughly equal: child support × years until kids are 18 + some buffer
100k for two kids until adulthood is reasonable baseline
Make sure beneficiaries are listed as your children directly (not ex-spouse)
This is more reliable than trying to save - you can't predict when something might happen
Can reduce coverage as kids get older and you build savings
Employer may offer group life insurance - check if you have this benefit
This is actually one of the most loving financial decisions a parent can make
commonMistakes: Dismissing life insurance as unnecessary expense
Not acknowledging the emotional complexity of divorced parent situation
Suggesting he should just save instead (can't save fast enough for unexpected death)
Recommending whole life insurance (much more expensive, unnecessary complexity)
Not validating his concern for his children's welfare
